native_encoding.metadata: Unary tags, payload lengths, variable count and indices.
native_encoding.coefficients: Binary magnitude bits individually encoded; unary term negation supplies signed integers.
rejection_conditions: Coefficient payload digit other than 0 or 1
Variable index outside declared finite tuple
Typed stack failure or final stack not exactly one formula
native_encoding.no_exponential_assembly: No duplication instruction; each operand subtree is consumed once.

algorithm: Validate all finite syntax and map malformed words to 0=1.
Emit the assembled formula and explicit existential prefix with binary variable names.
Preserve Boolean negation. Compile binary constants by linear-size Horner terms if only 0,1 are allowed.
For absent unary minus, use fresh uniquely determined value variables and conjoin arithmetic gate equations.
reductions.all_input_correctness: For every binary word w, native ETR(w) iff ordinary ETR(f(w)).

algorithm: Validate syntax/binding and map malformed source words to the native zero-variable falsum instance.
Drop unused variables and rename used identifiers densely; never expand a large binary label numerically into unary.
Normalize comparisons, signed constants and subtraction; compile to typed postfix.
Eliminate rational literals by fresh uniquely defined variables with nonzero-denominator equations conjoined outside all original Boolean contexts.
For explicit sparse exponents or arithmetic DAGs, add gate variables; repeated squaring costs O(log(e+1)) per exponent.
reductions.all_input_correctness: For every conventional source word s, ordinary ETR(s) iff native ETR(g(s)).

reductions.construction: Fresh arithmetic gate values and Boolean truth bits; truth-equivalent gadgets for equality and strict positivity; product intermediates reduce every constraint to degree at most two.
reductions.correctness: For each original assignment, truth iff existence of auxiliary real values satisfying all equations; both atom polarities are enforced.
reductions.warning: Displayed gated products must be flattened; before flattening they are not all quadratic. A single sum-of-squares equation is quartic, not quadratic.

boundary_checks.input: One occurrence of source label x_(2^k)
boundary_checks.result: Dense renaming avoids exponential unary-index expansion.
Its native natural record has exactly 2k+6 bits.

boundary_checks.input: Boolean negation around an equality or inequality
boundary_checks.result: Direct syntax preserves it; quadratic gadgets enforce both truth polarities.
False in native ETR, true for complex feasibility; existing negativeSquare theorem covers native rejection.

boundary_checks.input: Truncated unary suffix, bad payload, out-of-range variable or ill-typed program
boundary_checks.result: Native rejection; reduction emits a fixed unsatisfiable target.
The empty real tuple exists; truth is exactly the formula truth value.

boundary_checks.input: Explicit arithmetic DAG or binary exponent
boundary_checks.result: Use polynomially many gate variables; do not unfold exponentially large trees.

accepted_primary_boundaries.statement: ExistsR corresponds to BP(NP_R^0), with actual real guesses and constants 0,1.
BP(P_R^0)=P^PosSLP is in CH; digital nondeterminism does not provide arbitrary real witnesses.
AGS2026 HN and variety-counting upper bounds concern algebraic closures, including complex roots for rational coefficients.

rejected_transfers.reason: Neither deterministic real computation nor algebraic-closure feasibility covers existential real witnesses.
No such theorem is established by the cited PosSLP argument.

rejected_transfers.claim: Real-solution counting is in FP^CH by AGS2026
rejected_transfers.reason: Their counted variety is over the relevant algebraic closure; real solutions are a different restriction.

rejected_transfers.claim: Arbitrary real constants are permitted in the BSS identity
rejected_transfers.reason: The superscript 0 fixes the machine constants to 0,1.

rejected_transfers.claim: Succinct descriptions of exponentially many constraints are covered
rejected_transfers.reason: The reductions apply to explicitly finite polynomial-size input syntax, not succinct-ETR.

remaining_trusted_bridges: Both explicit syntax reductions and their finite-machine time bounds
Textbook BSS and ETR complexity-class identification

risk_assessment.judgment: The identified encoding and scope pitfalls have explicit resolutions. This is a bounded mathematical audit, not a calibrated probability estimate or a new formal equivalence proof.
